newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W.European new car figures present mixed picture.
newsitem.headline: W.European new car figures present mixed picture.

text.p: West European new car registrations in March fell three per cent year-on-year, presenting mixed signals for the region's markets, the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA) said on Tuesday.

Germany's Volkswagen kept a clear lead in combined market share for the 18 countries covered, despite posting zero growth year-on-year, capturing 17.2 percent or 213,400 units from a market totalling 1,241,100 vehicles.

Italy's Fiat Group, boosted by a national incentive scheme according to ACEA, grew registrations by 7.5 percent to snatch second position, a 12.8 percent market share, beating the combined figure of 12.6 percent for Japanese manufacturers.
Tightly bunched, with shares of 11.9, 11.2 and 11.1 percent respectively, came the United States's General Motors Group, France's PSA Group and the U.S.-owned Ford Group.
Of those, GM dropped 10.3 percent in units registered compared to March 1996 while Ford lost 9.3 percent and PSA, which comprises Peugeot and Citroen models, lost 7.4 percent.
While new incentives bumped up Fiat's figures, their removal hit hard for France's Renault, which lost 8.9 percent in units registered to post a market share of 9.6 percent.

National factors also affected Sweden's Volvo, ACEA's James Rosenstein told Reuters, where an end to uncertainties about government policy on company car taxation prompted a 40.5 percent rise in units sold, giving the Nordic carmaker a 1.8 percent market share.

"There's an up side and a down side to incentives," Rosenstein said, adding that on the one hand fleet renewals improved the European car park's environmental performance while on the other, the introduction and removal of incentives disrupted national markets and encouraged price wars.

"There's a lot of good in incentives because people get rid of their old bangers but it does tend to put a bit of a downward pressure on prices, because people get used to getting a hefty sum off the new car they are buying in return for their old one," he said.
Figures covered the European Union's 15 countries along with Switzerland, Norway and Liechtenstein.
ACEA's breakdown for national markets showed markets in Sweden and Italy grow 41.5 percent and 25.1 percent to 20,100 and 220,500 units respectively.
Of the other large markets, France slumped 21.1 percent to 151,400, Germany fell 8.6 percent to 343,000 while Britain was barely changed on 179,900.
